tools.name: check-package
tools.description: Checks whether a dependency (npm, PyPI, RubyGems or Packagist/Composer, or a GitHub Action used in a workflow) is on the DugganUSA malicious-package deny-list or has published advisories. Suited to a pre-install step in an agent or a CI pipeline, against slopsquatting and hijacked-package attacks.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search, enrich-ioc, stix-feed-summary, check-package · Private data: search, enrich-ioc, stix-feed-summary, ai-model-price, check-package · Public sink: search, enrich-ioc, kev-exploitation-stickiness · Destructive: stix-feed-summary.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search, enrich-ioc, stix-feed-summary, check-package · Private data: search, enrich-ioc, stix-feed-summary, ai-model-price, check-package · Public sink: search, enrich-ioc, kev-exploitation-stickiness · Destructive: stix-feed-summary

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
